principles: Optimize only after preserving MemoryFreshnessPack semantic parity.
Prefer bounded indexed lookup over whole-token-map scans.
Keep runtime memory advisory and never gate evidence.
Make performance claims only from full-profile machine evidence.
drivers: 1,000,000-record warm/cache path must pass indexedWarmCacheMs<=2000 before any 1-2s claim.
CLI process boundaries matter, so cache/index reuse must be durable or explicitly measured.

options.name: A: Profile-first indexed optimization with parity gate
pros: Targets known bottleneck while proving semantic equivalence.
Supports staged M0-M6 evidence and blocks false performance claims.
Can keep fallback paths for rare fuzzy cases.
cons: Requires more tests and benchmark plumbing before claiming DONE.
May need multiple optimization passes if first bottleneck moves elsewhere.

options.name: B: Replace matching with exact lookup only
pros: Smallest code change and likely fastest common path.
cons: Risks losing fuzzy/includes behavior and silently changing memory guidance.
Does not solve cross-process cache or durable hot path evidence.

options.name: C: Keep current implementation and only document report-first
cons: Does not satisfy the user-requested 1-2s optimization target.
Leaves the known token-map scan and process-local cache limitations unresolved.

chosen: A: Profile-first indexed optimization with parity gate
rationale: Choose profile-first indexed optimization because the user asked to complete M0-M6, not merely document limitations. This option preserves evidence discipline while giving the best chance to reach the 1-2s full-profile hot path target safely.

preMortem.scenario: Fast path silently drops fuzzy or superseded results.
preMortem.trigger: Exact lookup replaces includes matching without an equivalent fuzzy auxiliary index and parity guard.
preMortem.consequence: Runtime memory appears faster but forgets important lessons or surfaces wrong guidance.
preMortem.mitigation: M1 golden parity and full-profile digest parity must pass before M2/M3 can be marked done.

preMortem.scenario: Benchmark passes in one process but real CLI sessions remain slow.
preMortem.trigger: Only process-local Map cache is measured, so each new CLI invocation rebuilds or rescans.
preMortem.consequence: User still sees slow session_brief/handoff/story entry despite green tests.
preMortem.mitigation: M4 must prove durable cache or prebuilt index reuse across process boundaries with strict freshness binding.

preMortem.trigger: Docs or summary call the 1-2s target done while indexedWarmCacheMs remains above 2000ms or performancePolicy stays report-first.
preMortem.consequence: Proofbound repeats the false-DONE pattern the system is designed to avoid.
preMortem.mitigation: M5 performance smoke fails above target and M6 summary must state blocked/report-first unless the full-profile command passes.

preMortem.scenario: Optimization introduces stale or unsafe cache reuse.
preMortem.trigger: Cache key misses projectRoot, source digests, config digest, policy version, limits, or indexVersion.
preMortem.consequence: A stale memory pack is reused after facts changed.
preMortem.mitigation: Persistent cache keys must bind all required fields and stale mutation tests must force misses or safe stale classification.
